span.label: how associative learning changes the pattern of correlations between neurons, and what that does to population coding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether learning acts on emergent population properties that cannot be observed in single neurons
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: shows learning inverts the relationship between signal and noise correlations, but only for stimuli that guide behaviour, and that this improves population decoding increasingly with population size
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: when noise correlation runs opposite to tuning similarity, a downstream reader can subtract the responses of dissimilarly tuned neurons, cancelling the shared noise while adding the signal, so the same spikes carry more information
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: learning-driven changes to feed-forward synaptic weights (with excitatory-inhibitory noise cancellation) decorrelate similarly tuned neurons and preserve or increase correlation among dissimilarly tuned ones, producing the inverted correlation structure
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the trigger for the correlation change is the learned stimulus-to-action mapping (the motif signalling which port to peck), not reward pairing, familiarity or exposure, which were equated across motif classes
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: positively correlated noise between similarly tuned neurons impairs coding because pooling cannot remove shared noise without removing signal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: positively correlated noise between oppositely tuned neurons improves coding because subtraction removes noise and strengthens signal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: trial shuffling separates the contribution of single-neuron plasticity from that of correlation change, since it leaves individual responses untouched
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the design equalises reward across all trained motifs so only the stimulus-response association differs
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: testing each motif in isolation confirms the behavioural asymmetry is about which response the motif signals, not about reward
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The narrow-spiking (putative interneuron) sample was too small for reliable pair analysis, so the population results rest on wide-spiking pairs only.
span.note: what this limits: every pairwise-correlation result: WE FOCUS ON WS NEURONS ... BECAUSE OUR SAMPLE OF NS NEURONS WAS NOT SUFFICIENT (N = 17 PAIRS FROM 36 SINGLE NEURONS) TO PERFORM RELIABLE ANA[lysis]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The claim that correlation-structure plasticity is confined to putative excitatory neurons is underpowered.
span.note: what this limits: the cell-type specificity claim specifically: THIS SUGGESTS THAT THE PLASTICITY ... PRIMARILY EXISTS WITHIN WS (PUTATIVE EXCITATORY) NEURONS, ALTHOUGH MORE DATA ARE NECESSARY - the negative half rests on the underpowered sample
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Recordings were made under urethane anaesthesia, unlike the awake comparison study, and the circuitry producing the stimulus-specific flexibility is not identified.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison with the awake primate study: A METHODOLOGICAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN OUR STUDY AND THAT OF (GU, ET. AL. 2011) IS THAT WE USED ANESTHETIZED ANIMALS WHILE GU AND COLLEAGUES USED AWAKE ANIMALS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The local or extrinsic circuit mechanism controlling the correlation structure remains to be established.
span.note: what this limits: any circuit account of the effect: FURTHER EXPERIMENTS WILL BE NECESSARY TO ELUCIDATE THE CIRCUITRY THAT YIELDS THIS STIMULUS-SPECIFIC FLEXIBILITY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: narrow-spiking neurons were excluded because the sample was too small for reliable analysis
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - narrow-spiking neurons were excluded because the sample was too small for reliable analysis, so the population results are the broad-spiking ones

span.label: recordings were made under urethane anaesthesia, unlike the study whose result this contradicts

span.label: contradicts → the inference from earlier work that stimulus-reward association drives auditory cortical plasticity
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS TASK RELEVANCE OF THE STIMULUS. 'ONLY THE TASK-RELEVANT motifs - those that birds learned to associate with a particular pecking location - elicited neural population activity with a NEGATIVE relationship between signal and noise correlations. In contrast, task-irrelevant motifs ... elicited neural population activi[ty]' [with the opposite sign]. The sign of the correlation relationship depends on learned relevance, so a claim about signal-noise correlations is only well-formed once the stimulus class is stated. Q-447.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: confirms → the theoretical prediction that changing the sign of the signal-noise correlation relationship could underlie attention or learning

span.label: noise correlation —contrasted-with→ signal correlation
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS DETERMINES THE SIGN OF THE EFFECT, NOT ITS SIZE. 'NOISE CORRELATIONS CAN EITHER ENHANCE OR IMPAIR CODING FIDELITY, DEPENDING ON HOW THE NOISE CORRELATION RELATES TO TUNING SIMILARITY (KNOWN AS SIGNAL CORRELATION) FOR EACH PAIR OF NEURONS.' A claim that noise correlations help or hurt is not well-formed until this relation is stated - so two papers reporting opposite effects can both be right, and a join on `noise correlation` alone would make them contradict. Q-476. · strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: correlated noise IMPAIRS coding between similarly tuned neurons and IMPROVES it between oppositely tuned ones. the same edge has opposite consequences depending on the second variable
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · task-relevant —contrasted-with→ task-irrelevant
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span said the motifs were heard equally often. This sentence names both AND GIVES THE DIFFERENTIA - 'the primary DIFFERENCE ... was thus the learned association between motifs and explicit behavioral choices' - so the contrast carries what it consists in. — strength of the relation: 1 — matched on familiarity and reward by design, differing only in whether the motif signalled a response - which is what makes the comparison interpretable

span.label: For motifs that had guided the birds' choices, the usual positive coupling between signal and noise correlation was inverted to a negative one.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Equally familiar but behaviourally uninformative motifs, and never-heard novel motifs, retained the canonical positive coupling, so the inversion was specific to task relevance rather than to exposure or reward.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The mean level of noise correlation itself did not differ between motif classes, so the learning effect lies in the correlation structure rather than in correlation magnitude.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The magnitude of signal correlation was likewise unaffected by task relevance.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Correlations improved decoding of task-relevant motifs more than of the other classes, confirming that the restructured correlations translate into better discrimination.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The coding benefit conferred by correlations was flat with population size for irrelevant and novel motifs but grew steadily with population size for task-relevant motifs.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Single-neuron firing rates showed only a small learning effect, much weaker than the population-level effect.
